explanation: Ants stroke aphids with their antennae to make them release honeydew. In return they drive off attackers such as ladybird larvae, much as herders protect their livestock.

claims.text: Ants tend aphids, protecting them and collecting the honeydew they release.
Bees, wasps and ladybirds do not tend aphids; ladybirds and their larvae eat them.
Ants stroke aphids with their antennae to prompt them to release honeydew.
Ants defend aphids against predators such as ladybird larvae.
